entities.evidence: Resen is the city located between Nineveh and Calah.
Nineveh, named in the preceding verse, is the first landmark used to locate Resen.
Calah, named in the preceding verse, is the second landmark used to locate Resen.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:12 as evidence for definite-object on the Hebrew particle at word index 0.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite direct object, here a city identified by name.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:12 continues the list begun in 10:11. וְאֶת רֶסֶן introduces the last city built.

analysis.evidence: וְאֶת רֶסֶן adds Resen to the cities governed by וַיִּבֶן, “he built,” in Genesis 10:11. The following phrase בֵּין נִינְוֵה וּבֵין כָּלַח locates Resen between Nineveh and Calah.
analysis.morphology: וְ is the coordinating conjunction “and.” אֶת is the unsuffixed form of the direct-object particle אֵת.
analysis.sense: Marks the named city רֶסֶן as a definite direct object.

draft.change: Append the place name רֶסֶן at word index 1 with the sense city-of-resen. Its relationship to the homographic noun meaning “rein” is unknown.
draft.definition: Resen, a city between Nineveh and Calah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:12 names Resen as an object of the building verb in Genesis 10:11 and gives its location.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:12 locates רֶסֶן with בֵּין נִינְוֵה וּבֵין כָּלַח, “between Nineveh and Calah.” Its place in the list of cities built in Genesis 10:11–12 identifies it as a city name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת marks it as a further direct object of וַיִּבֶן, “he built,” in Genesis 10:11.
analysis.sense: The city between Nineveh and Calah.

analysis.evidence: בֵּין נִינְוֵה וּבֵין כָּלַח locates Resen between Nineveh and Calah. The marked בֵּין introduces Nineveh, the first of the two places.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a place-name article under the name’s own consonants, נינוה.
draft.definition: Nineveh, a city named among the places built in Genesis 10:11.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:11 lists Nineveh as an object of “built.”

analysis.evidence: בֵּין נִינְוֵה וּבֵין כָּלַח locates Resen between Nineveh and Calah. Nineveh is the first of the two landmarks.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בֵּין נִינְוֵה וּבֵין כָּלַח locates Resen between Nineveh and Calah. The marked וּבֵין introduces Calah as the second endpoint.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ ‘and’ is prefixed to the preposition בֵין ‘between’.

draft.change: Add a place-name entry for כָּלַח with the gloss “Calah,” correcting the source gloss “wages.”
draft.definition: Calah, a city named in the account of the building of Nineveh and Rehoboth-Ir.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:11, וְאֶת כָּלַח completes the list of places governed by וַיִּבֶן.

analysis.evidence: The phrase בֵּין נִינְוֵה וּבֵין כָּלַח locates Resen between Nineveh and Calah. כָּלַח names the second place in that pair.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Calah, a city listed alongside Nineveh and Rehoboth-Ir.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:12 as evidence for the existing city sense of עִיר in article 3yr.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:12, הָעִיר הַגְּדֹלָה describes a named settlement as “the great city.”

analysis.evidence: The verse locates Resen between Nineveh and Calah, then describes a place as הָעִיר הַגְּדֹלָה, “the great city.”
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes עִיר, a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state. The attributive adjective הַגְּדֹלָה agrees with it in gender, number and definiteness.

analysis.evidence: In הִוא הָעִיר הַגְּדֹלָה, “it is the great city,” the adjective describes the city's size.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a feminine singular absolute adjective agreeing with הָעִיר in gender, number, and definiteness.
